mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-60.4 to -50.7) alongside steady WORKPLACES recovery, indicating an established reopening trajectory that will continue to push retail and recreation activity upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -60.4 to -50.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the established monotonic recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has been declining each week (19.4 to 16.0). Once RESIDENTIAL falls below a threshold of 15 points, reduced home-bound behavior will translate into a surge of discretionary retail and recreation trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15.0 points in a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 19.4 to 16.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses below 15.0 but RETAIL_REC mean over the subsequent two weeks does not increase relative to the prior two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES (-49.3 to -45.3) and TRANSIT (-60.0 to -55.1) signals restored commuting infrastructure usage; when both rise together, trip-chaining behavior (commute plus errands) compounds to lift RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved over the last three weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise concurrently but RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks fails to exceed its prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under a continuing reopening policy regime, relaxed restrictions on non-essential retail combined with easing PARKS gathering limits create compounding permission effects that lift RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks, as consumers resume previously-restricted shopping and leisure trips.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded to 40.3 at t-0w after a dip to 27.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: Policy regime remains in reopening phase but RETAIL_REC mean over the next two weeks declines relative to the prior two weeks despite continued PARKS strength.

mechanism_narrative: High summer PARKS mobility (40.3% above baseline) indicates households are substituting outdoor leisure for indoor retail and recreation trips during favorable July weather, causing RETAIL_REC growth to stall or dip over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds 35 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from 27.1 to 40.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: PARKS remains above 35 points but RETAIL_REC over the next week rises rather than falls relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near -17 points for two consecutive weeks after earlier declines, suggesting essential-trip behavior has normalized; this stabilization frees up discretionary trip budget, raising RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within 2 points of its prior week value for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM measured -17.4 then -17.3 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes as specified but RETAIL_REC over the next week does not increase relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility functions as a one-week leading indicator for RETAIL_REC because transit trips to commercial districts precede recorded footfall; the recent TRANSIT improvement (-57.1 to -55.1) predicts a near-term rise in RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -57.1 to -55.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves week-on-week but RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: If a new tightening regime were triggered by rising case counts, a sudden reversal in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declines combined with a rebound in RESIDENTIAL would signal renewed restriction, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next four weeks despite its recent recovery.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT drop more than 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises more than 3 points
failure_condition: The specified reversal in WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL occurs but RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks still increases relative to the prior four weeks.
